description: spa_refresh mirror can ship an embedded SPA with index.html but ZERO hashed assets: remove_stale_entries deletes before copies land, and two overlapping 'just up' runs race the shared dist dir. Evidence 2026-08-25: instance healthy + CLI green while every asset 404'd. Mitigations landed: just-up flock lock (tmp/just-up.lock) and post-deploy smoke (scripts/smoke.nu, fails just up on any red route incl. every index-referenced asset). Structural fix (atomic swap + post-condition) open in fabro-332e.
resolution: partial: lock + smoke guard deployed; atomic swap open in fabro-332e

content: Post-deploy smoke runs as part of 'just up' and aborts the pipeline on any red probe

name: spa-crash-safe-publish
description: Crash-safe SPA publish (fabro-332e, commit ba8e5277c): spa_refresh publishes via ordered phases — additive copies, index.html flip LAST (only file referencing hashed assets by name), stale removal after; per-file temp+rename atomic replace; verify_index_references guards mixed staging snapshots pre-publish AND post-publish; SpaRefreshLock (tmp/fabro-dev-spa.lock, pid + /proc stale-break) serializes refresh across processes. When touching this path: keep the ordering contract, never delete-then-copy into the embedded assets dir.

name: zigbuild-warning-fixes
description: just-up zigbuild warnings fixed (2026-09-08): (1) 'ignoring deprecated linker optimization setting 1' is a zig 0.13 + rustc linker_messages false positive (rust-lang/rust#158192) — rustc passes -O1 linker arg on opt-level>=2 release builds; silenced with #![allow(linker_messages)] (reason attr) in lib/apps/fabro-cli/src/main.rs, remove when upstream filters it. (2) proc-macro-error2 future-incompat (E0365 'pub use proc_macro', rust#127909) came via rust-embed -> include-flate 0.3.2; fixed by 'cargo update -p include-flate' (0.3.4 switches codegen to proc-macro-error3 3.1.1 which has the 'pub extern crate proc_macro;' fix).

Stale-binary trap: file-tool edits in the run sandbox leave edited sources with epoch (1970-01-01) mtimes, so cargo considers rlibs/test binaries fresh and nextest runs old code — symptoms are logically impossible contradictions (a pure-function assert passes in the same process while the gate using it fails). Fix on sight: stat the touched source vs target/debug/deps timestamps and 'touch' every edited file before rebuilding (run 01M2TJ9JZGE42JNBJ22A258MBZ, fabro-e566 implementer, ~4 wasted diagnostic calls).
resolution: touch edited sources before rebuild; verify with stat source-vs-binary mtime when test results contradict the code

description: Stale cargo test binary after edit_file changes: nextest reused a prior compile whose fingerprints did not register the edit (run 01M1YBBXR99PNME6Y8ZED4Y2NN, fabro-fb16) — panic line numbers pointed 7-14 lines away from the actual asserts and two tests failed on a code path the source no longer contained.
resolution: touch the edited file (or cargo test --no-run) to force recompilation before trusting a failure diagnosis; after the forced rebuild both tests passed unchanged.

description: Stale test-binary near-miss (run 01M2NP2W92HHF3QAH17F42GZ5K, seed fabro-b959): after edit_file changes to lib/apps/fabro-server/src/server/automation_scheduler.rs, a cargo nextest run reported a panic at a source line whose content no longer matched the panic message — cargo had not rebuilt (0.5s Finished, test binary reused), so a correct fix evaluated as still failing for two runs.
resolution: Check panic line/content against current source before re-deriving root cause; force touch + rebuild when inconsistent

description: Stale nextest binary after symlink-path edits: after editing publish.rs via /workspace/fabro (symlink to /repos/denkhaus/fabro), cargo nextest kept failing with an old assertion until 'touch' forced a rebuild. If a nextest result contradicts freshly verified source logic, touch the file and re-run before debugging.
resolution: touch the edited file before re-running nextest when results contradict verified source

description: nextest ran stale test binaries after source edits (fabro-4ebd run 01M2R1KKXXG2KZ63F3XT31WT71): two consecutive runs reported union/wire-test failures that vanished after 'touch <test file>' forced a rebuild — the pass/fail verdict came from a pre-edit compiled binary. When a nextest failure contradicts a just-passed isolated run of the same test, force a rebuild (touch the source or cargo clean -p <crate>) before debugging the code.
resolution: diagnosed as stale cargo test-binary caching; workaround: touch the edited source or cargo clean -p <crate> before rerunning; root cause in cargo/nextest fingerprinting unresolved

content: Rerun nextest only after 'touch <changed-file>' when a snapshot or test-source fix appears not to take effect; identical failure line numbers across runs indicate a stale binary, not a bad fix. Observed twice in the v0.348.0-nightly.0 upstream merge (attach.rs, inspect.rs).
